name: פונקציה מעריכית 9^x – הקלט עבור פלט נתון (באנגלית)
questiontext:
A function \( f : R \rightarrow R\) is defined by the rule

\[ f(x) = {{CT:0}}. \]

Which input of the function \(f\), has the output {{CT:1}}?

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write both sides of \(9^x={{CT:2}}\) as powers of 3 and compare the exponents.
Step 1 — The equation
To find the input, we need to find the value of \(x\) for which

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}}. \]

Step 2 — Both sides as powers of 3
Since \(9=3^2\), the law \(\left(a^m\right)^n=a^{mn}\) gives \(9^x=3^{2x}\).[[if test="{{CT:6}}"]] The right-hand side is also a power of 3:

\[ {{CT:2}}=3^{{{CT:3}}}. \]

[[else]] The right-hand side is also a power of 3, with a negative exponent because \(\dfrac{1}{a^{k}}=a^{-k}\):

\[ {{CT:2}}=\frac{1}{3^{{{CT:4}}}}=3^{{{CT:3}}}. \]

[[/if]]So the equation becomes

\[ 3^{2x}=3^{{{CT:3}}}. \]

Step 3 — Compare the exponents
The function \(t\mapsto 3^t\) is one-to-one (strictly increasing), so equal powers of 3 have equal exponents:

\[ 2x={{CT:3}}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x = {{CT:5}}. \]

Check: \(9^{({{CT:5}})}={{CT:2}}\). Hence the input is

\[ x = {{CT:5}} \]

on_false.feedback: The value of the function for your input is \({@ev(9^(ans1),simp)@}\) which is not equal to {{CT:1}}.
